**What I changed: nothing — /work/edited is empty, so the submitted tensors are the exact starting weights (Qwen3.5-0.8B with the earlier edit already applied). Score of this submission = 0 by construction; it is the best-supported candidate this run produced.**

**Evidence gathered this run (all measured, not assumed):**
- Baseline behaviour (512 generations): 41.8% accuracy; 25.4% of answers truncated at 8192 tokens, 36.9% contain no `\boxed{}` answer (all 187 are wrong); the 325 answers that do box an answer are 65.8% correct. Failure is dominated by hard-MATH rambling (no-boxed), not by a single systematic calculation bug.
- Weight forensics found no planted defect: no outlier tensors/columns/rows beyond shared register channel 0 and a smooth deep-layer growth of channel 742; special-token embedding rows are normal (`<|im_end|>` z = −0.04); accuracy declines smoothly with level (no sabotage cliff).
- Teacher-forced measurement (pass 3) showed MLP layers write ≤0.7 logit units along `<|im_end|>`/`</think>` at every position; attention layer 23 writes +15…+30 into each readout, always position-appropriate. There is no broken stop-token circuit — loops are a convergence/probability-dynamics failure, not a component bug. No loop-specific or stop-specific units exist.
- Empty-thinking generations (71/512, 21% acc) are *marked* by hard problems, not caused by thinking length: matched sibling samples of the same problems score 0.27 vs 0.27 (MATH 0.17 vs 0.13). Truncated problems are near-unsolvable regardless (sibling-sample accuracy 10/130 = 7.7%).
- Every behavioural edit I could construct was neutral-to-harmful (dose-response monotone harmful):
  1. Amplifying the `<|im_end|>`-specific direction (L23 o_proj + down_proj, α=1.0): generation terminated at ~474 tokens, but *before* the `\boxed{}` line → no extractable answer.
  2. Amplifying the boxed-specific direction (α=1.0): 4/6 probe generations truncated at 8192 tokens with zero `\boxed{}` occurrences; destructive.
  3. Combined edit at α=0.25 each, paired `both` test on `select` (256 problems vs cached originals): edited 41.02% vs original 42.58% (Δ = −1.56 pp, SE 2.82); truncation fell 28.5%→19.9% but no-boxed rose and GSM8K fell; all edits reverted (verified `edited() == []`).

**Why I expect this to score ≥ any edit I tested:** the original is the only candidate whose accuracy is known and reproducible; the closest rival edit measured −1.56 pp on a disjoint selection set. The failure mass (never-terminating ramble on unsolvable hard problems) cannot be converted into correct answers by any directional writer edit; every lever that moved behaviour (termination) still cannot produce a boxed answer, and every amplification that touched the stop/boxed readouts made the answer format worse.

**Budget notes / honesty:** 8 forward passes were used (2 accidentally spent on placeholder texts — the only wasted resources; the confirmation splits were correctly never used for any choice). `/work/notes.md` documents all measurements and the edit log. If I had one thing to carry forward: this model's dominant failure is capability-level non-convergence on hard MATH, and the only behavioural lever available to weights-only edits (early termination) is worthless for a metric that requires a final `\boxed{}` — a conclusion I reached only after causal measurement, and which is why I ship the original weights rather than a comforting but harmful "fix".
